resources.string: Epididymal duct
Epididymis · Posterolateral view with the testis partly cut away
Efferent ductules
These small channels lead from the rete testis into the head of the epididymis, where they feed into a single epididymal duct.
Head of the epididymis
The broad head caps the upper pole of the testis and receives the efferent ductules.
Body of the epididymis
The narrower body runs behind and to the side of the testis. It contains many turns of the same continuous epididymal duct.
Tail of the epididymis
At the lower pole of the testis, the coiled duct in the tail straightens and continues as the vas deferens, which turns upward.
Vas deferens route
Vas deferens · One-sided route from the epididymis to the back of the bladder
Spermatic cord segment
The vas deferens ascends from the epididymal tail within the spermatic cord, alongside vessels and nerves.
Inguinal canal
The spermatic cord passes through this short passage in the lower abdominal wall. The vas deferens leaves the cord at the deep inguinal ring.
Pelvic segment
After entering the pelvis, the vas deferens runs along its side wall and turns toward the back and base of the bladder. It does not open into the bladder.
Ampulla of the vas deferens
This widened end of the vas deferens lies medial to the seminal vesicle. It joins the duct of that vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct on the same side.
Paired seminal vesicles
Seminal vesicles · Posterior view at the bladder base
Blind upper end
The upper end of each seminal vesicle is closed. It lies behind the bladder and lateral to the end of the vas deferens.
Coiled gland
Each vesicle is a coiled glandular tube. Its folded lining secretes fluid that contributes to semen.
Seminal vesicle duct
This short outlet leaves the lower end of the gland and joins the ampulla of the vas deferens on the same side. The channel beyond the junction is an ejaculatory duct.
Ejaculatory duct cutaway
Ejaculatory ducts · Posterior projection through the prostate
Duct junction
On each side, a seminal vesicle duct joins the ampulla of the vas deferens. The single narrow channel below each junction is that side’s ejaculatory duct.
Course through the prostate
The paired ducts enter at the base of the prostate and angle inward and forward toward the urethra, remaining separate as they cross the gland.
Openings at the seminal colliculus
The two ducts empty through separate openings at the seminal colliculus, a raised landmark on the back wall of the prostatic urethra.
Prostatic urethra
This part of the urethra runs from the bladder neck through the prostate. The ejaculatory ducts empty into it rather than continuing as separate channels below the gland.
